title: Gartner: Choosing the Right Approach for Application Modernization and Cloud Migration
overview: This July 2024 supplementary note selects modernisation approaches by root cause. Diagnose the six business and IT drivers, identify whether technology, structure or functionality needs change, then compare rehost, replatform, rearchitect, rebuild and replace. Retain, encapsulate and retire remain valid alternatives; apply choices incrementally by component.
big_ideas: Five main approaches, in rising scope: rehost (lift and shift), replatform (lift and reshape), rearchitect (refactor), rebuild (rewrite), replace (buy COTS/SaaS).
Alternatives when modernizing isn't worth it: retain (leave as is), encapsulate (wrap in an API), retire (decommission).
Each approach changes different layers: rehost/replatform fix technology; rearchitect fixes technology and architecture; rebuild/replace can also change functionality.
Diagnose first using six drivers: business fit, innovation and agility (business); cost, complexity and risk (IT).
Map drivers to root cause: cost, complexity and risk point to technology; business fit and innovation point to functionality; agility and complexity point to architecture.
Pick the approach that fixes the causing layer with acceptable value, time to value, disruption, cost of change and risk; don't expect replatforming to improve business fit.
Modernize incrementally, component by component, not as a big bang; different components may need different approaches.

sections.title: Why the choice of approach matters
sections.summary: States the note's key findings and recommendations, gives survey evidence that modernization spending is rising, and explains why picking the wrong approach is costly.

notes.h: Pick from the problem, not fashion
items: **Common mistake** → leaders **modernize or migrate** without establishing **why the app obstructs the business**
**Result** → the chosen approach **misses the root cause**
**Apps lose** → **business fit**, **innovation support**, **agility**
**Apps get** → **costlier**, **more complex**, **riskier**
**Cause-effect analysis** using **six drivers**
**Evaluation framework** to **choose per application**

notes.lead: Modernization is not always cloud migration; most efforts involve cloud, but:
items: **COBOL app** → **rearchitected to Java** and **stays on the mainframe**
**Or replaced** by an **on-premises COTS package**

terms.def: Improving an existing application's technology, architecture or functionality so it better supports the business.
Commercial off-the-shelf software bought from a vendor rather than built.

check.q: A CIO launches a 'move everything to cloud' modernisation programme because competitors are doing it. Eighteen months later, costs are up and the business sees no benefit. What did Gartner's note warn about?

items: **Warning**: choosing an approach from **fashion** without first **diagnosing** why each application **obstructs the business**
→ the chosen approach **misses the root cause** → **overruns**, **late delivery**, **little benefit** or a **cancelled programme**
**Fix**: a **cause-effect analysis per application** using the **six drivers** before picking an approach

check.q: A bank's COBOL system must be modernised, but the mainframe contract runs for 8 more years. A teammate says modernisation is impossible until they can move to cloud. Do you agree?

items: **Rearchitect** the **COBOL** code to **Java** and stay on the **mainframe**
Or **replace** the app with an **on-premises COTS package**
a.foot: Pick the approach from the **drivers**, and treat the **hosting location** as a **separate decision**.

check.q: A board member cites a survey showing CIOs plan more spending on modernisation and cloud and less on legacy infrastructure, and asks to fund all applications equally. What is the flaw?

items: **The trend explains why** portfolios need attention: apps **lose fit and agility** while growing **costlier and riskier**
**But** it doesn't say **which apps need what**
**No one-size-fits-all** fix → **fund by application** after **diagnosis**
Some will need **rebuilding**, some only **replatforming**, and some should be **retained** or **retired**

sections.title: The five approaches and what each can change
sections.summary: Defines the five approaches, covers which application layers each can change, lists the three alternatives for legacy apps, and introduces the two diagnostic questions.

items: **Rehost** → **moves infrastructure**
**Replatform** → **changes runtime** with **minimal compatibility edits**
**Rearchitect** → **restructures existing code** while **preserving behaviour**
**Rebuild** → **rewrites** it, possibly **like-for-like**
**Replace** → adopts **COTS or SaaS**
notes.foot: Compare the **affected layer** before comparing **implementation cost**.

items: **Rehost, replatform** → change **technology only**
**Rearchitect** → changes **technology and architecture**; **limited value for functional problems**
**Rebuild, replace** → can change **functions and features**, and also **technology and architecture**

notes.lead: When modernization is not worth it, usually decided in a portfolio assessment.
items: **Retain** → **leave as is for now** (**too much effort or risk**, or **near retirement**)
**Encapsulate** → **expose data and functions as services** through an **API** while **hiding the internals**
**Retire** → **decommission**, often as **part of a replace**

notes.h: Rehost vs rebuild in one line
items: **Rehost** → **cheapest** and **least risky**, but **changes almost nothing**
**Rebuild** → **most flexibility**, but **costs the most** and carries the **most risk**

terms.def: 'Lift and shift': redeploy to other infrastructure without changing code or features.
'Lift and reshape': move to a new runtime platform with minimal code changes for compatibility, but no structural or feature changes.
Re-engineer/refactor: restructure the code without changing external behaviour, to remove technical debt and improve non-functional qualities.
Wrap a legacy app's data and functions behind an API so they can be reused without changing the internals.
Retain: leave as is for now. Retire: decommission the application.

check.q: An app's code and features are fine, but it runs on middleware that is going out of support. Which approach fits, and why not rebuild?

items: The problem is in the **technology layer** → replatforming changes it with **minimal code edits**
**Rebuilding** would also change **architecture** and **functionality** that don't need fixing → adds **cost**, **time** and **risk** for **no extra benefit**

check.q: A legacy claims engine is valuable and stable, but changing it is very risky, and a new mobile app needs its data. Modernise or one of the alternatives?

items: Expose its **data and functions** as **services** through an **API** → the mobile app can use them
The implementation stays **hidden and untouched**
**Extends the app's value cheaply**
a.foot: The **engine's limits remain**, so revisit it later if **business fit** or **agility** becomes the driver.

check.q: A team proposes rearchitecting an app into microservices because 'users say it is missing features'. Will rearchitecting fix that?

items: **Rearchitecting** changes **technology and architecture** while **preserving behaviour** → limited value for **functional problems**
**Missing features** point to **functionality** → **rebuild** or **replace** can change it
Rearchitect only if the real complaint is the **speed or risk of adding features**, which is an **agility** problem

sections.title: Six drivers, root cause and the selection framework
sections.summary: Describes the three business and three IT drivers of modernization, maps them to the application layer most likely causing the problem, and presents Gartner's framework rating each approach.

sub: **Agility** → **cannot keep pace with change** at **acceptable cost and risk**
**Complexity** → hurts **maintainability** and the **cost and risk of change**
**Risk** → **security, compliance, supportability, scalability**, **skills shortage on old platforms**

notes.foot: Usually **a mix of both** tips the decision.

items: **Technology** → often contributes to **cost, complexity or risk**
**Functionality** → **business fit** or **innovation**
**Architecture** → **agility** or **complexity**
**Probable links**, **not a one-to-one diagnosis**
**Evidence** may reveal **more than one layer**

notes.h: Choose the approach that changes that layer
items: **Technology faults** → **rehost, replatform or rearchitect**
**Architecture faults** → **rearchitect** (or **rebuild**)
**Functionality faults** → **rebuild** or **replace**

notes.lead: Each approach rated on value, time to value, disruption, cost of change and risk.
items: **Rehost** → **low on all of them**
**Rebuild** → **most flexible** but **highest cost and risk**
**Replace** → **high value** with the **greatest business disruption**

terms.def: Business fit, innovation, agility (business) plus cost, complexity, risk (IT).
Accumulated shortcuts and outdated design that make an application costly and risky to change.

check.q: A system can't support a new digital sales channel. What must you diagnose before choosing an approach?

a.lead: Diagnose: missing **business functionality**, or missing **access to existing functions**?
items: **Functionality missing** → **rebuild** or **replace** the component that needs it
**Functions exist but can't be reached** by the new channel → **encapsulating** them behind **APIs** or **integrating at the architecture level** may be enough

check.q: Releases of a core app take months and often break unrelated features. Rearchitect or rebuild?

items: **Slow, risky change** points to **agility** and **complexity** → usually from the **architecture**
**Rearchitecting** fixes **architecture and technology** at lower **cost**, **risk** and **disruption** than a **rebuild**
a.foot: **Rebuild** is justified only if the **functionality must also change** or the code **can't be restructured**.

check.q: Running costs of an app are too high for its value, but users are happy with it. Which drivers and layer does this point to, and which approaches would you shortlist?

items: **Driver**: **IT cost**
**Layer**: most likely **technology**, such as **expensive licences** or **over-provisioned infrastructure**
**Shortlist**: **rehost** or **replatform** → low on **cost**, **risk** and **disruption**
**Not** rebuild or replace: would add **disruption** and **risk** to fix **functionality that already works**
a.foot: **Check the evidence**: drivers **suggest a cause** but don't diagnose it **one-to-one**.

check.q: A sponsor prefers replacing an in-house HR system with SaaS because it has 'the highest value'. What does the framework add to that view?

items: **Replace**: can change **all layers** and offers **high value**, but causes the **greatest business disruption** → **processes redesigned**, **users retrained**
**Rehost**: low on **value**, **cost**, **risk** and **disruption**, but **changes little**
a.foot: Choose replace only if **business fit** or **innovation** is the driver **and** the business **accepts the disruption**.

steps.label: Six drivers
steps.detail: Three business drivers and three IT drivers; usually a mix.

steps.label: Root-cause layer
steps.detail: Drivers suggest likely layers; confirm the actual cause in technology, architecture or functionality before choosing.

steps.label: Approach
steps.sub: one that can change that layer
steps.detail: Technology issues: any of the five approaches can change technology. Architecture issues: rearchitect, rebuild, replace. Functionality issues: rebuild or replace (rearchitect has limited value).

sections.title: Weighing consequences and the incremental approach
sections.summary: Lists the considerations to weigh when shortlisting approaches and recommends modernizing component by component.

items: **Potential business value** → **often overestimated** (e.g. expecting a **replatform** to improve **business fit**)
**Time to value**
**Business disruption** → **retraining**, **process redesign**; **SaaS replacement is high**
**Cost of change**
**Execution risk**
**Shortlist approaches** that address the **actual problem**
**Compare** → **outcomes, disruption, time, cost, execution risk**
**Choose a proportionate change** rather than the **most extensive** one
**Target** can be a **component** rather than a **whole app**
**Gartner recommends** → **component by component** rather than **big bang**
**Different components**, **different approaches** → some a **rebuild**, others just a **replatform**

terms.def: How long before the modernization starts delivering business benefit.
Modernizing an application component by component rather than all at once (big bang).
Retire the app and repurchase the capability as COTS or SaaS.

check.q: A large app needs a new customer workflow, but its stable reporting module only needs a supported runtime. Must the whole app be rebuilt?

items: **Workflow component** → **rebuild** or **replace**, where functionality must change
**Reporting module** → **replatform**, where only the **runtime** is the problem
**Confirm dependencies** and **sequence the work** → each change delivers its benefit and **risk stays contained**

check.q: A sponsor expects replatforming the ERP to make it fit the business better. How do you respond?

items: **Replatforming** changes only the **technology layer** → won't improve **business fit**, which is a **functionality** problem
Gartner: **potential value is often overestimated** in this way
**Set expectations**: if business fit is the driver, **rebuild** or **replace** is needed, with their **higher cost, risk and disruption**

check.q: Two approaches both fix an app's diagnosed problem: replatform (3 months) and rebuild (14 months, more flexibility). The business wants value this year. Which, and why?

items: Fixes the **actual problem** with **shorter time to value**
**Lower cost of change** and less **execution risk**
Choose a **proportionate change**, not the most extensive one
a.foot: **Rebuild's extra flexibility** is worth it only if a **near-term need for functional change** is expected.

exam_angles.q: A government agency's 20-year-old COBOL benefits system costs too much to run, is hard to change, and its COBOL staff retire within 3 years. The benefit rules themselves still meet policy. Recommend a modernisation approach using the drivers and root-cause layers.

a.lead: **Rearchitect**, for example to **Java**, possibly staying on the current platform.
items: **Drivers**: **cost**, **complexity**, **agility** and **risk** (a **skills shortage** on an **old platform**)
**Root-cause layers**: **technology** and **architecture**, not **functionality**, since the **rules still fit**
**Rearchitecting** **preserves behaviour** while addressing these problems
**Rebuild** only if **restructuring isn't viable**
**Execution**: modernise **component by component**; **encapsulate stable parts** behind **APIs** where **new channels** need them
**Before committing**: compare **time to value**, **cost**, **risk** and **disruption**
a.foot: The **skills deadline** sets the **order of the work**.

exam_angles.q: An on-premises web application has three complaints: hardware is ageing, the database needs constant hand-tuning, and features take months to ship. Compare rehost, replatform and rearchitect for moving it to cloud, and say which complaint each one fixes.

items.t: **Rehost** (**lift and shift** onto **cloud VMs**) → fixes **ageing hardware**
sub: Quickly, cheaply and with the **least risk**

items.t: **Replatform** (e.g. a **managed database** or **managed runtime**, **minimal code changes**) → also fixes **database operations**
**Rearchitect** (e.g. **refactoring into services**) → the only one that fixes **slow feature delivery**

a.foot: **Sensible plan**: **replatform now** and **rearchitect** the **slowest-changing components later**.

exam_angles.q: A company wants to replace its 12-year-old custom CRM with a SaaS product. The sales team is attached to custom workflows. Using Gartner's framework, what should it consider before deciding?

items: **Check the drivers** are **business fit** or **innovation**: replace is justified for **functional gaps**, not for **technology problems** that **replatforming** could fix more cheaply
**Replace**: **high value** but the **greatest business disruption** → **sales processes redesigned**, **users retrained**, **custom workflows may be lost**
**Weigh** **time to value**, **cost** and **execution risk** with **stakeholders**
**Plan** **data migration** and the **retirement** of the old CRM

exam_angles.q: Describe a structured method for selecting modernisation approaches across a 150-application portfolio, and show how it would avoid the failures Gartner describes.

items: **Portfolio assessment**: decide whether each app is **retained**, **retired**, **encapsulated** or **modernised**
**For candidates**: define the issues with the **six drivers**; trace each to its likely **root-cause layer** (**technology**, **architecture** or **functionality**), **checking the evidence**
**Shortlist** approaches that can **change that layer**
**Weigh** **value**, **time to value**, **disruption**, **cost** and **risk** with **stakeholders**
**Execute incrementally** per **component**
a.foot: Avoids **fashion-driven choices** that **miss the root cause** (→ **overruns** and **little benefit**), and avoids **big-bang rewrites**.
